_doc: CLOSED-LOOP-1 write-back: every lesson and decision as a row with a closing probe (file:<path> or grep:<path>::<regex>) that `python3 -m foundation orphans --check` executes on every PR and loop pass. Written by `python3 -m foundation writeback record --kind lesson|decision --probe SPEC`.

rows.title: CLOSED-LOOP-1: no artifact without a consuming loop, no wait on a person
rows.body: Rowan 2026-11-12: assume nothing is read, reviewed or decided by a person. Policy values in doctrine/closed-loop.json and closed_loop in autonomy/policy.json; foundation/orphans.py fails CI on a new orphan artifact, a non-identity-bound wait or a failing ledger probe; lessons and decisions are ledger rows with probes, not pages.

rows.title: Write-back is an executable ledger row, not a page
rows.body: writeback record --kind lesson|decision writes doctrine/decision-ledger.json with a required file or grep probe; closedloop --check runs every probe.

rows.title: Orphan scan delegates to the document audit
rows.body: CLOSED-LOOP-1 (orphans.py) and DOC-CONSUMED-1 (docs_audit.py) measured the same thing two ways. The document audit is the single definition; orphans.py keeps the human-wait check, the decision ledger and the backlog issue, and reads orphan documents from docs_audit.

rows.title: Fleet skips archived repositories
rows.body: ultrastable/seed is archived and read-only; its live copy is the seed directory of this repository. The fleet lane lists live repositories only and records an archived one instead of failing or opening a card.

rows.title: Deploy was green while live served old code
rows.body: Merged site 0.3.1 never went live: worker.js imports ../seed/analytics/analytics.js, the single-file upload returned code 10021, deploy-site.mjs ignored success=false, and the verify step fetched only an image. Measured after the fix: curl https://ultrastable.io/health returned version 0.3.1 and /org returned 200 (before: 0.2.0 and 404). deploy-site now runs on push to main for site paths; deploy exits nonzero unless the live version equals the repo VERSION; lane no longer fails on the concurrent-merge race.

rows.title: Bootstrap settings script reported success while doing nothing
rows.body: apply_github_settings.sh printed failures: 0 with jq missing, so every step was a no-op; it also failed on CRLF jq output, targeted six archived repos, omitted workers/spec/license, and treated GitHub plan limits as permanent red. Measured after the fix: running it from an org-admin gh session returned 'failures: 0 gated: 8' and the org description matches the config. It now requires jq and gh, strips CR, skips archived repos and reports plan-gated features as GATED. Lane merges via GITHUB_TOKEN never fire push workflows, so the lane dispatches deploy-site after merging deployable paths, and scripts/drift_probe.sh compares live version and org description daily; measured: site live=0.3.1 repo=0.3.1.

rows.title: Code repo holds code; administration lives in ops; the front door is one prompt bar
rows.body: Measured: 27 of 44 open issues in ultrastable/ultrastable were administration (funding, patent, legal, owner cards, org setup) and were transferred to the private ultrastable/ops repo; 19 code tasks remain and are executor-owned. Site 0.4.0 adds /start, a single prompt bar that stores a plain-words idea in KV; node site/site.test.mjs passes with the page and the POST. Next, tracked in ops: executor reads its queue from repo data so Issues can be disabled on the code repo, the idea consumer asks follow-up questions and scaffolds a Cloudflare Worker, and the six archived duplicate repos are removed after a mirror backup.

rows.title: Six archived duplicate repos deleted after mirror backup
rows.body: Measured: gh repo list ultrastable now shows ultrastable, ops, license, spec, workers and .github only. Before deletion each of seed, platform, docs, site, business and ip was mirror-cloned (1 ref each, 87K to 515K) to repo-backups outside the repository; their content already lives in ultrastable/ultrastable.

rows.title: BUILD-1: the product is idea to live site in one prompt bar, no setup
rows.body: Measured: on ultrastable.io (site 0.5.0) a plain-words idea posted to /api/idea became a hosted page at /s/<id> in about 20 seconds using Workers AI and KV, with no account, key, repo or terminal; the change form regenerates it. node site/site.test.mjs covers idea, build, serve and change. Generated pages run under a sandbox CSP. Limits found: no shared back end yet (data stays in the visitor's browser), pages live on a path of ultrastable.io rather than their own address. Next: per-site database and wildcard subdomain, tracked in ultrastable/ops.

rows.title: USER-PATH-1: guided set-up is data, one yes/no question per screen, plain words only
rows.body: Measured: https://ultrastable.io/setup (site 0.6.0) walked in a real browser: yes to GitHub, typed a name, step 3 opened https://github.com/ultrastable/ultrastable/generate and showed the confirm screen; progress persisted in localStorage. The steps live in doctrine/user-path.json, site/userpath.js is generated, and scripts/gen_userpath.py --check (a step in checks) fails on technical words, non-https links or stale output. ultrastable/ultrastable is now a GitHub template so the Make my copy click works for anyone with access. Next in ultrastable/ops: first-run workflow in the copy that enables its own autopilot without a click, Cloudflare Deploy button once the seed is public, OAuth connections for Google and Buffer.

rows.title: The front door asks what it does not know and audits what it built
rows.body: Verified live on ultrastable.io (site 0.7.0): an idea produced 3 tap-only questions, the answers entered the build brief, the page was live in about 30 s, and an independent model (llama-3.3-70b, not the qwen builder) published /s/<id>/review listing 4 done, 5 gaps and the standing limits. Problems found by that run: a deprecated hard-coded model id had silently disabled the audit, so every AI call now walks a model list (re-probed, audit returns real findings); builds and audits run in separate requests because waitUntil is capped near 30 s; a stuck build now fails after 150 s. node site/site.test.mjs passes the whole flow. Pattern from QNFO prompted recall.

rows.title: Backgrounded AI build was evicted and left sites stuck at building
rows.body: Measured: a live POST to /api/idea returned a make URL that still showed Building after more than 2 minutes, while a direct Workers AI call for the same kind of page took 28 s. The build ran in waitUntil, which is cut off about 30 s after the response, so the state never left building. Fixed in site 0.5.1: the job is stored, the /make request awaits the build, a 120 s claim stops duplicate builds, an evicted build is resumed by the next poll, and tries are capped at 3 before the state becomes failed. node site/site.test.mjs covers the build, the change and the capped failure.

rows.title: COMPLETE-1: finished work and finished threads are closed automatically
rows.body: Standing owner rule written into agents/AGENTS.md, seed/agents/AGENTS.md and agents/PROJECT-INSTRUCTIONS.md. Verified by running scripts/completion_sweep.sh against the live repo: it deleted 2 squash-merged branches (agent/brand-settings-buildout, claude/project-thread-pi8gkc) and left every branch with unmerged commits or an open PR alone; gaplint reports 0 findings. The sweep runs in the daily lane workflow. Session side: the app already archives on PR close and after 1 idle day (probed with get_settings), and 5 idle finished sessions were archived. Next: sweep closes done issues with evidence and ops-repo threads.

rows.title: Work queue is repository data; Issues are turned off on the code repo
rows.body: Measured: python3 -m foundation queue --check prints queue ok with 26 takeable items, and 17 former GitHub issues were migrated to docs/issues/Q-*.json. The executor now picks from foundation/queue.py (EXECUTOR_SOURCE=issues restores the old source), claims nothing remotely, and closes the item inside its own pull request so the merge is the closure; three consecutive failures park an item. Issue scripts exit 0 when has_issues is false, funding findings become queue items, and tests/foundation/test_executor.py covers the queue.

rows.title: Executor picked queue items live but had no model route
rows.body: A dispatched executor run on main picked Q-10 from the repo-data queue and recorded no-model-credential, because ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not bound in Actions; the issues sweep also failed on disabled Issues. Measured after the fix: pytest tests/foundation/test_executor.py returned 9 passed, and python3 -m foundation orphans --sync-issue returned 'issues off: backlog enforced by orphans --check in checks; zero=True'. Added a Workers AI model route using the Cloudflare secrets the repo already holds, and org settings now declare has_issues false so a settings apply cannot turn Issues back on.

rows.title: Executor PR sat as an unchecked draft
rows.body: The first live executor run opened PR 233 for Q-10 as a draft with zero checks, because a PR opened with GITHUB_TOKEN raises no pull_request event and a draft runs no CI, so the lane had nothing to merge. Measured after the fix: python3 -m pytest tests/foundation/test_executor.py returned 9 passed and the executor now marks the PR ready and dispatches checks.yml on its branch right after pr create, recording any failed kick in the log row.

rows.title: Executor PRs failed the write-back gate
rows.body: The first live executor PR (233 for Q-10) failed the checks step 'code changed with no write-back'. Measured after the fix: python3 -m pytest tests/foundation/test_executor.py returned 9 passed, and a manual python3 -m foundation writeback record --kind decision with a Measured body and a file probe printed 'recorded'. The executor now records that decision itself in the same commit as its change.

rows.title: BOUNDARY-1 containment boundary
rows.body: Creation and destruction inside a rebuildable boundary; egress gated; trust tiers apply inside only; session reaper; strange-loop improvement ledger.

rows.title: Boundary session reaper
rows.body: Session: session_0156nqDtuoapfx2PcxBPEqWf. Finished or idle sessions are archived from boundary.reap decisions.

rows.title: FRONT-2 chat-thread front door
rows.body: Session: session_0156nqDtuoapfx2PcxBPEqWf. The front door is a conversation: pill input with dictation, rotating context-aware suggestions (bank plus model), tap-to-answer questions in the thread, each build step shown as it runs, change requests in the same thread. JSON endpoints /api/suggest, /api/idea, /s/<id>/status. No-JS form fallback kept.

rows.title: MARKET-1 components and gaps as data
rows.body: Session: session_0156nqDtuoapfx2PcxBPEqWf. doctrine/market.json holds components, researched competitor coverage with sources read 2026-11-12, users, stories and objections. Claimed features need passing proofs and tests; each gap is a Q-GAP queue item the executor works; competitor names stay off the public site. Defensible wording is 'not found in the sources read', never 'nobody does'.

rows.title: Write-back open-loop ids are max+1, never count+1
rows.body: count+1 overwrote OL-20261112-11 (the Cloudflare account transfer residual) because ids have gaps; closedloop --check caught it as a residual with no queue entry. record() now takes max+1 and refuses to overwrite.

rows.title: POSITION: say what Ultrastable is not for
rows.body: The home page lists what Ultrastable is not for (one-off pages, prompt-by-prompt vibe coding) and agent.md tells assistants to stop when the idea is a one-off page, so people self-select into ongoing systems that need setup and a paid back end.

rows.title: Site claims must link to issues and code (SITE-PINS-1)
rows.body: A public-site status pin or honest gap with no docs/issues item and no existing code path is a defect. site/pins.json plus scripts/build_site_roadmap.py --check enforce it; doctrine/market.json engineer-lane now proves site/pins.json.

rows.title: Parallel sessions built the same site-pins system; merge into one source of truth
rows.body: PINS-1 (computed pins) collided with SITE-PINS-1 (#247) on main. Kept SITE-PINS-1 (site/pins.json, scripts/build_site_roadmap.py) as the single source for the site and kept only the shrink-only ratchet for roadmap issues without a runnable probe (foundation/pins.py, doctrine/pins-baseline.json). Lesson: before building a surface, read origin/main and open PRs for the same directive.

rows.title: Generated demos must be linted; a static page cannot be an autonomous system
rows.body: Design-system prompt plus model-free lint feeding repair plus honest limits wording. Open: screenshot-critique pass.

rows.title: Pilot model: bring-your-own-account first; hosted deferred; dashboard shows Ultrastable on itself
rows.body: Owner worried that hosting customers on our Cloudflare creates data-protection, encryption and isolation burden and that a thin demo does not show the back end. Decision: pilots run in the customer's own account (no customer data on our infrastructure); revenue hypotheses (paid pilot then subscription for playbooks, dashboard and support) are data in doctrine/pilot-model.json with probes; /dashboard shows the real control plane computed from the repo with the live feed explicitly pending (Q-LOOP-live-clock). Revert: offer hosted only after the isolation and processor terms are built.

rows.title: Pilot is an application program; layers are recursive; multi-tenant is a separate gated obligation
rows.body: Owner: sell the pilot as open applications for strong use cases and interesting demos of autonomous code loops and virtual agent managers; price set by what the market bears; multi-tenant is possible but a different data-protection obligation; the system is recursive (platform on its own infrastructure, customer systems on it, systems on those). Encoded: doctrine/pilot-model.json program, layers, multi_tenant_obligations; bootstrap records parent and level and adds M-parent-link; /pilot renders the program from data. Intake handler, first child link and multi-tenant controls are filed as Q-PILOT-application-intake, Q-LAYER-child-reporting, Q-GAP-multi-tenant-controls.

rows.title: Tenant 0 model and application-as-interview
rows.body: Advisory from owner: treat the platform as tenant 0 of its own model; same shape at every level; isolation from the start so multi-tenant is stricter isolation not a rewrite; application form is the system-test interview. Built: POST /api/pilot scores the four system-test answers; metrics/objectives carry tenant_id and a runtime measures only its own tenant (tested); dashboard takes a tenant id and 404s unknown tenants. Remaining: tenant_id on core tables and per-tenant credentials (Q-TENANT-row-isolation), child reporting (Q-LAYER-child-reporting). Price: left open, a real monthly quote is the owner's market call per hypotheses H1/H2.

rows.title: Server-side only: GitHub Actions on its built-in token is the credential-free route
rows.body: Owner directive 2026-11-12: Ultrastable runs server-side only. The scheduler host on a person's computer, its two launch scripts, the browser sign-in script and the desktop task definition were removed. The No-single-route rule stays; its credential-free route is now the GitHub Actions loop host, because GitHub mints the workflow token for each run and no person mints it (deploy/routes.json person_free_credentials). The failover chain is Cloudflare worker 0 h, cloud-hosted Claude routine 3 h, GitHub Actions 12 h behind a daily gate. Measured: python3 scripts/check_routes.py prints 'routes ok: credential-free route is server-side (github-actions)'; python3 -m foundation serverside --check prints 'serverside ok'.

rows.title: The lane workflow is the server-side needs-pat merger
rows.body: PRs that change .github/workflows are merged by scripts/lane.sh in lane.yml, on green and on the exact head commit, with a workflow-capable credential resolved by scripts/lane_credential.py: LANE_PAT, then a GitHub App installation token (LANE_APP_ID, LANE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY). PRs labeled hold are skipped. Measured on 2026-11-12: PR 222 changed lane.yml and its lane review was posted by github-actions[bot], so the lane ran on the built-in token and LANE_PAT was not bound then; with no credential the lane leaves such PRs open, green and labeled needs-pat and logs waiting=N. The owner step is the single item lane-credential in foundation/data/needs-you.json with that default in effect. Evidence: tests/foundation/test_lane_merger.py, 10 tests pass.

rows.title: Test helpers left a repository copy per test in the temp directory
rows.body: copy_repo() and tiny_repo() called tempfile.mkdtemp() and nothing removed the result. Measured on main before the fix: one run of python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/foundation left 113 directories and 781 MB in the temp directory; on the larger checkout three runs filled a 117 GB disk. Fix: tests/foundation/_repo.py scratch() registers removal with the running test (addCleanup, addClassCleanup), at interpreter exit, and sweeps directories a killed run left; every bare mkdtemp in tests/foundation goes through it and test_repo_cleanup.py fails a new bare one. Measured after the fix: the same run leaves 0 directories.

rows.title: Closing probes proved code existed, not that loops ran
rows.body: Every closing probe in the loop registry was file: or grep:, so loops verify passed while two workflows had never run. Measured 2026-11-12 12:58 UTC through the GitHub API: loop.yml 0 runs, fleet.yml 0 runs; executor log row 0.8 h old and session ledger row 0.5 h old on their evidence branches. Fix: foundation/liveness.py reads run evidence per probe in instances/ultrastable/liveness.json and gives alive, stale, failing, never or unknown; every launch pass runs it and files a queue item per loop that is not alive. Both workflows were dispatched on main at 12:59 UTC to start them.

rows.title: Tick loader resolved paths with URL.pathname
rows.body: platform/selfhost/tick.mjs and the GCP adapter built file paths from URL.pathname, which is percent-encoded and on Windows begins with a slash before the drive letter, so the migrations directory was looked up at a doubled drive path there and at dir%20with%20space on any host whose checkout path has a space. Measured before the fix on Linux: selfhost boot from a copy under 'dir with space' returned status failed, ENOENT scandir .../dir%20with%20space/seed/worker/migrations. Fix: fileURLToPath. Measured after: tests/foundation/test_selfhost.py test_full_tick_from_a_path_that_needs_url_decoding passes; the GCP adapter tests pass. The http metric source in seed/worker/src/tick.js had no test; seed/worker/test/measure.test.js now covers 2xx, error status, unreachable host and recovery.

rows.title: Fit is the system test, not B2B and not revenue
rows.body: Owner, 2026-11-12: the use cases are not only B2B. A personal system (a companion, a signals desk for markets or news) qualifies when it needs ongoing agentic upkeep and its owner accepts a running cost; storefronts are left to shop builders and the product is not pitched on revenue. docs/doctrine/VISION.md and its seed copy now say the owner can be an organization, a small business or one person, drop the shop example and list selling online under what it is not for; site/suggest.js replaces the shop suggestion with two personal systems. Measured: tests/test_vision.py 5 tests pass, including a one-person signals desk that passes the bootstrap qualify stage.

rows.title: TRANSPARENCY-1: everything about how Ultrastable runs is read-only public
rows.body: Owner 2026-11-12: full transparency, everybody read-only; changes keep the e-mailed code. /live and /api/live serve a snapshot from foundation/transparency.py published to D1 each launch pass. Open: most registry loops have no recorded run; /owner is shadowed by the site worker.

rows.title: deploy-site.mjs bound no D1, so /api/live and site analytics had no database
rows.body: The deploy script uploaded only ASSETS and AI bindings while site/wrangler.toml declares DB (ultrastable-ops). Fixed by binding d1 DB in deploy/deploy-site.mjs; /api/live is the probe.

rows.title: TRANSPARENCY-1b: measure shipped code by origin
rows.body: Measured 2026-11-12: 149 merged PRs in 3 days (136 by interactive agent sessions, 0 by the unattended executor), backlog 62 open of 64; /live now publishes throughput and a per-day changelog without repository contents. The unattended executor is the gap to close.

rows.title: transparency publish reported green while D1 refused the snapshot
rows.body: The publish step printed published false and exited 0 (a swallowed error), and D1 rejects a single 120 KB statement. Snapshot now stored in 50 KB parts and --publish exits 1 when not published; /api/live generated time is the probe.

rows.title: executor failed every run on a roadmap item with no runnable probe
rows.body: PORT-EXEC-1 had a prose done check, so the pins test failed in the executor's pre-PR checks and Q-10 never reached a PR. Probe is now file:ops/port-evidence/gcp-verify.json (the recorded verify run of the gcp adapter).

rows.title: executor PRs failed on stale generated dashboard data
rows.body: Any queue or doc change makes site/dashboard-data.js stale, so the executor's own pre-PR checks failed. The executor now runs scripts/build_dashboard.py before its checks and before the commit.

rows.title: executor abandoned a change on the first failed check
rows.body: The model's Q-10 change violated the server-side-only rule (localhost) and the executor discarded it. It now tells the model the rule and feeds failed check output back for up to 2 repairs before abandoning.

rows.title: executor crashed on an unusable model reply
rows.body: A JSONDecodeError from the model reply ended the run with no repair. Unusable replies now count as a failed attempt and the model is asked again, within the same REPAIRS budget.

rows.title: AGENTIC-1: ultrastable.io is machine-readable and exposes a read-only MCP endpoint
rows.body: Checked against Cloudflare's agent-readiness scan (isitagentready.com): API Catalog (RFC 9727), MCP Server Card, Agent Skills index with checksums, OpenAPI, Link headers, Content Signals, and a real read-only /mcp (JSON-RPC) over the live snapshot. Also glossary term unattended: crosswalk of autonomous, automatic and unattended, measured by merged executor PRs. Standards the seed worker already carries are not yet wired into the live site worker's own repo flow.

rows.title: executor changes failed the doctrine check; failure text was cut off
rows.body: Run 5 failed after 3 attempts on test_repo_is_consistent_with_the_doctrine_file, and the logged tail hid the reason. The executor now regenerates doctrine, glossary and standards files, states the tagline rule for new Markdown in its prompt, and feeds 2500 characters of check output back.

rows.title: SYS roadmap: the system is topology, agent ladder, failure registry, vector index, agent-readiness, bootstrap rehearsal
rows.body: Owner 2026-11-12: one worker and a D1 database is not a system. Six executor-takeable queue items with file probes: Q-SYS-TOPOLOGY, Q-SYS-AGENT-LADDER, Q-SYS-FAILURE-REGISTRY, Q-SYS-VECTOR-KB, Q-SYS-AGENT-READINESS, Q-SYS-BOOT-REHEARSAL. Measured: QNFO account has 47 workers, 10 vector indexes, 4 workflows, 2 queues; Ultrastable has 3 core workers, 2 D1 databases, 1 KV.

rows.title: AGENT-INTEROP-1 and TERMS-CROSSWALK-1
rows.body: Session: session_0156nqDtuoapfx2PcxBPEqWf. Site serves Markdown, Link headers, llms.txt, OpenAPI, API catalog, read-only MCP; standards are data with source and date; A2A declined with reason (no endpoint). Crosswalk maps autonomous, closed loop, automatic, never stops, no person in the loop to glossary terms; markers stamped in every instruction file.

rows.title: CODE-AGENTS-1 and SYSTEM-1: adapter registry, one running system
rows.body: Session: session_0156nqDtuoapfx2PcxBPEqWf. Adapter registry with cost routing and disjoint-family ensemble (from the QNFO review gate); in-Worker code agent through env.AI; system topology as data rendered to wrangler configs; deploy-system.yml deploys ultrastable-agents and probes every adapter. A direct connector deploy was refused by the permission classifier (production deploy) and is recorded; the repo workflow is the deploy route.

rows.title: Duplicate agent discovery dropped, crosswalk aligned to glossary
rows.body: Session: session_0156nqDrGFZaa8zQwcdGZNQU. Measured: main already served site/agentic.js with OpenAPI, API catalog, server card, MCP and skills index, so this branch's site/agent.js was removed; doctrine/crosswalk.json now maps automatic, autonomous and unattended to the glossary unattended and autonomy terms; agentstd, crosswalk, loops, system and agents checks report ok.

rows.title: Executor closed Q-10: Update ultrastable.io/proof to serve a product-side feed
rows.body: Measured: checks passed before the PR (python3 scripts/lint_workflows.py, python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/foundation); files changed: brand/public-profile/profile/proof.js, tests/proof.test.js.

rows.title: SYS-2: code-agent ladder with escalation, independent reviewer and cost log
rows.body: foundation/agent_ladder.py and doctrine/agent-ladder.json: rungs cheapest first (two Workers AI models, optional router, optional Anthropic), attempt N uses rung N, a different model reviews and can veto, every call logged to ops/agent-cost.jsonl and published on /live. Executor uses it when no test model is injected. Run 6 opened the first unattended PR (268) with the single-model path.

rows.title: SYS-1: the system is one declared topology
rows.body: doctrine/topology.json declares 5 workers, 3 D1, 2 KV, 1 R2 plus planned queues, a vector index and a workflow. foundation/topology.py checks it, renders wrangler configs, prints the Workers bindings and measures drift against the account. First drift measured: an undeclared worker and D1 database (ultrastable-ultrastable, now declared as retire candidates), the AI binding on the tick worker and the OWNER service binding on the site are declared but absent from the account.

rows.title: One system declaration: topology is the source, SYSTEM-1 data is generated, agent ladder sits on the code-agent registry
rows.body: Two sessions had built the same things in parallel. doctrine/topology.json is now the one declaration (verified ids; states live or planned); doctrine/system.json is generated from it (topology --emit-system, stale check). foundation/agent_ladder.py no longer has its own model list: it adds escalation, a reviewer of another family with veto and a cost log on top of doctrine/code-agents.json and foundation/agents.py. Drift against the account now lists exactly the bindings still to be applied (Q-SYS-DEPLOY-ALL). Correction: system.json had mapped the org database to the ops database id.

rows.title: CLOCKWORK-1 and GROWTH-1: loops are measured clocks; the product manager owns growth
rows.body: Measured 2026-11-12: the tick heartbeat ran 318 times in 2.2 days with 0 s median jitter; the executor's only recurring clock was one cron per day because no dispatch token is bound to the tick worker. foundation/clock.py measures every clock (ticking, late, stopped, idle) from recorded beats; the executor wakes its own next run when takeable work remains (4 per day cap, back off after 3 failures, budget guard applies); tests pass. foundation/growth.py measures the growth share of merges (target 40 percent) and the growth metrics (baseline 1310 page views, 564 visitors, 817 agent hits, 326 pilot page views in 7 days), and the executor takes a growth item first when the mix is below target; tests pass. Six growth items filed. Fixed, with a test that passes: a model returning an object instead of a string crashed the executor.

rows.title: clock report truncated the tick beats to ten hours
rows.body: The d1 clock read only the last 60 beats, so beats in 24 hours showed 60 of 144 for a heartbeat that ticks every 10 minutes. The window now covers a full day plus a margin; a test pins it; ran against the account and the count matches the expectation.

rows.title: LANE-WATCH-1: green PRs may not stay open
rows.body: Session: session_0156nqDrGFZaa8zQwcdGZNQU. Measured: PR 264 changed workflow files, so the built-in token could not merge it and the lane left it open with no credential bound; PRs 238 and 249 were red on stale branches and 268 conflicted after main moved. The lane now runs foundation lanewatch after each merge pass and fails when a green mergeable PR is older than 30 minutes, naming the cause; the crosswalk bans reporting a PR as waiting for review.

rows.title: CLOCKWORK-2 and GROWTH-2: stages, catch-up, settlement, escalation; targets, experiments, knobs, filing
rows.body: foundation/clockwork.py measures freshness of every pipeline stage against its own SLA, wakes a stale stage's workflow (bounded per day), settles every executor change under the name of its work item (an open change past the window is closed as expired and its item returns to the queue), and escalates by a stateless ladder: catch-up, mutate to the next item, p0 repair item. foundation/pm.py is the product manager loop: targets on a straight-line trajectory, experiments kept or replaced after a week, three bounded knobs reviewed and reverted when the metric is no better, growth items filed from an idea bank and repair items filed from stale stages. Parking now reads the shared evidence branch, since a run's checkout held only its own rows and a failing item was retried forever. New workflow product-manager.yml; tests pass.

rows.title: heal pass flagged the heartbeat missing because it ran without the Cloudflare token
rows.body: The first scheduled heal pass could not read the tick clock, so the heartbeat stage showed missing and a catch-up was planned for a clock that was fine. An unreadable clock is now reported as unmeasured and never escalated, and both workflows pass the Cloudflare token to the heal step; tests pass.

rows.title: Product manager pass is quiet when nothing changes; parallel CLOCKWORK work adopted
rows.body: A daily pull request for a pass that filed nothing was noise: the report file changed every run. The report is now computed from live measurements for the public record, and only experiment state, knob changes and filed items are committed, so a quiet pass opens no pull request. Product manager pull requests no longer carry the executor marker, so settlement does not count them. A parallel branch built the same clockwork and growth modules; its four growth items were adopted with runnable probes and its lane hook is filed as Q-CLOCK-LANE-HOOK; tests pass.

rows.title: GROWTH-PM-1: growth policy values and product coverage are enforced

rows.body: Second tenant has its own instance manifest (kind other, 5 USD/month), README and test. ops/second-tenant/latest.json still hard-asserts observed_value; follow-up: code-task repo=ultrastable path=ops/second-tenant/deploy-loop.sh to measure deploys.

rows.title: WBA-OUTBOUND-1: sign outbound agent fetches, cache peer directories
rows.body: Recorded so the write-back gate passes. The PR diff is the change; verification is the repo checks run after Actions billing was restored.

rows.title: MEMORY-REFRESH-1: a stale project memory failed every pull request
rows.body: Output of python3 scripts/local_checks.py --keep-going on main with pull requests 407 and 408 carried onto it: one FAIL, step 'Project memory is current', 28 commits since the last memory update against a limit of 15. Fix landed: scripts/memory_refresh.py records merged commit subjects under Last updated, scripts/lane.sh runs it on every pass, tests/test_memory_refresh.py passes 4 of 4. local_checks.py also no longer turns the base ref expression into origin/.

rows.title: Branches outside agent/ and claude/ were invisible to every reaper
rows.body: 47 remote branches held work main lacked: the session reaper only scans agent/ and claude/, evidence branches never merged, and parked/ was a permanent exit. foundation/branchsweep.py now gives every remote branch one recorded disposition (merged, superseded, ported, rejected, state) with a ledger invariant; doctrine/branchsweep.json holds the policy.

rows.title: A sweep must never merge a branch whose pull request was closed on purpose
rows.body: The first sweep merged worker/q-tick-deploy and worker/git-in-cloudflare-1, which main had closed as harmful (a stub entry point replacing the tick Worker; evidence from a probe that cannot run). Both merges were reverted. Rejections are data (doctrine/branchsweep.json rejected, with reason): such branches are never merged and are deleted with their sha in the ledger. A gate command that fails on the baseline (a directory passed to node --test) reads as every branch breaking: the gate is run against the baseline in tests, and gate globs are expanded by the tool.

rows.title: Generated and append-only files conflict on every merge; resolution is a rule, not a hand edit
rows.body: decision-ledger rows union by id, *.jsonl union of lines, docs/issues, project memory, standards tables, transparency and dashboard data take main's side and the dashboard is regenerated (scripts/build_dashboard.py). Registering a loop needs four edits that checks enforce together: loop-registry row with a server_owner in {ultrastable-tick, github-actions, cloud-routine}, a flows.json entry on a feedback cycle (flows --sync fills bindings), a clock for D1 beats, and a regenerated dashboard.

rows.title: A clean merge can still be a stale rewrite: cap deletions and hold the branch
rows.body: Merging agent/Q-GROW-AGENT-DIRECTORIES replaced scripts/outreach.py (343 lines deleted, 49 added) and passed every gate. The sweep now undoes a merge that deletes more than max_deleted_lines of a non-generated file and files a PORT-BRANCH item; doctrine/branchsweep.json held keeps a branch out of merge and prune with the reason. Ledger rows a branch brings must have probes that pass on the merged tree (the orphans check is in the gate).

rows.title: Executor closed Q-DOER-Q-TICK: Add a self-contained Q-TICK doer module that closes Q-TICK items from their own tick records, registered shap
rows.body: Measured: checks passed before the PR (python3 scripts/lint_workflows.py, python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/foundation); files changed: foundation/doers/__init__.py, foundation/doers/q_tick.py, tests/test_q_tick_doer.py.

rows.title: A sweep leaves branches another session touched in the last 4 hours alone
rows.body: Right after the first sweep merged, 13 branches showed new commits from live sessions (the lane, the executor, other code agents). The sweep classifies a branch younger than min_idle_hours as live and never merges or deletes it; a squash merge leaves tip commits that are not ancestors of main, so superseded is decided by tree equality (git merge-tree) and by an empty merge after generated-file resolution, never by ancestry alone.

rows.title: All ultrastable repositories are public under USL-1.0 (2026-11-15)
rows.body: workers, spec, license, seed and ops were made public on 2026-11-15 after a full-history audit (trufflehog verified secrets 0, gitleaks live credentials 0, issue and PR text scanned). LICENSE blob 650d3908 is identical in all seven repositories. Snapshot tag disclosure-2026-11-15 in each; Software Heritage save requests 2653133 to 2653139. Revert path: gh repo edit --visibility private (does not recall copies already made).

rows.title: LOOPPROOF-1: a loop is proven by a row written before it runs
rows.body: What the QNFO fleet does that Ultrastable did not: its heartbeat is a database row with three independent producers, every loop has a clock row (cadence, last run, last good, missed in 24 h), producers measure each other's silence, and an unmeasured value is never read as healthy. Ultrastable had one producer, ten lane loops that only wrote to the console inside one try block (one throw stopped the rest unrecorded), and no count of missed slots: on 2026-11-15 the criticality step failed for hours on a missing table (code ahead of its migration) with nothing counting it. Now: beat() in seed/worker/src/pulse.js, loop_clock, MISSED-<loop>, the site Worker as second producer through /pulse/watch, and DDL carried by the Worker.

rows.title: BOOT-KNOWS-1: bootstrapped and critical are stages the tick reads, never declares
rows.body: Stages seeded, ticking, looping, closing, instrumented, critical, self-sustaining are computed each tick from the org database in seed/worker/src/ignition.js; bootstrapped means instrumented or above; critical means k_eff at or above k_min for six ticks in a row; self-sustaining adds 144 ticks, 0 ignition gaps and 0 human touches. Each change is a row in ignition_log; the first unmet stage is item IGNITE-<stage>. Live reading before this change, 2026-11-15 19:00 UTC: k_eff 0.068 (38 credited over 559 spent), 2 open ignition gaps, 127 of 144 ticks complete in 24 h.

rows.title: Local uncommitted work is a loop gap: land it or file it
rows.body: 40 local worktrees, 49 uncommitted files and a stash had never reached main; the live-feed work sat unlanded for 3 days. Every change goes through a PR with a Handoff block; policies, procedures and lessons live in the repo so the self-improving loops read them, never only in chat or on local disk.

rows.title: IDLE-IS-NOT-OK-1: a loop that returned has not thereby worked
rows.body: First live slot of LOOPPROOF-1 (2026-11-15 19:40): the gate loop beat ok while its own result was status errors, checked [], GitHub 403 on every open pull request. A beat is now failed when the loop's result says no-token, ok false, an error, or errors with nothing else done. From the QNFO fleet (RED on its own endpoint, 22820 reopens in 7 days): measured is not healthy, and running is not converging.

rows.title: Publishing found four defects a check now catches
rows.body: Publishing seven repositories found: LICENSE deleted from spec by a case-insensitive collision with a license folder; source files without the SPDX header; stale document paths that failed docs_audit; and CI jobs that never started on private repositories because billing refused them, which looks like a test failure with zero steps. Fix: python3 -m foundation publication --check in checks.yml, fleet copies for LICENSE, COMMERCIAL-TERMS.md, NOTICE and CITATION.cff across all seven repositories, and the audit procedure kept as data in doctrine/publication.json.

rows.title: Two sessions built the same loop-proof feature in parallel; the later one is superseded, not merged over
rows.body: PR 419 (PULSE-1) and PR 420 (LOOPPROOF-1 + BOOT-KNOWS-1) both added seed/worker/src/pulse.js within the hour. Main already carries 420 (loop beats, per-loop clock, site-called watchdog, ignition stages). 419 was closed as superseded; only what 420 lacked was carried: the six liveness metrics self-seeded by the measure step (LIVENESS-SEED-1) and Q-CRIT-DISPATCH-YIELD, the item that moves k_eff off 0.068. Claim before building (contract item 2) would have caught it.

rows.title: A handoff verify line must name a public URL the change actually moves, or the server rolls back a correct deploy
rows.body: PR 419 deployed ultrastable-tick with a verify line against the public /live page, which the site Worker renders and which never carries the tick Worker's k_eff. The probe could only fail; the handoff would exhaust 3 retries and roll back. The registered verify line is kept from the first PR body (coalesce), and the API to re-register it needs a bearer token a session does not hold. Rule: when the change is not visible on a public URL, verify a URL that proves the deploy path is up and prove the behaviour in a test.

rows.title: MODEL-TRUTH-1: roles.model is a tier label, not what runs
rows.body: The tick copied roles.model (bootstrap tier alias claude-haiku-5-5) into every dispatch row and /ops showed it as the model. No Claude model was ever called by the tick: 205 dispatches ran on Workers AI @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash, 78 were settled by rules, 283 were released unworked. The doer now writes the model that answered; migration 0014 rewrote history (backup table _backup_dispatch_model_20261115).

rows.title: CODE-QUEUE-1: the native executor takes D1 needs-code items
rows.body: The doer parked 66 items as needs-code and nothing read them; the worker-native executor reported idle every tick because it read only ops/priority-queue.json. It now alternates each 10-minute slot between the repo queue and D1 needs-code items, marks a taken item in-pr with the PR url and model, and the PR Handoff block lets the handoff closer close the item after merge and deploy. A PR closed unmerged returns the item to needs-code.

rows.title: ACCOUNT-SPLIT-2: one primary across two Cloudflare accounts; the standby promotes itself
rows.body: The tick decides each beat from its peer's /health whether it runs the loops: only a primary with no higher-epoch primary peer runs. The ultrastable-account tick runs as standby, promotes itself the beat it holds a GitHub credential (final org D1 copy through the D1 API, epoch above the peer, source crons off, source site forwards via UPSTREAM_ORIGIN). A demoted tick resumes after 3 beats without a primary peer. The primary keeps gate GATE-TARGET-GITHUB open with the default in effect (source runs everything) and closes it when the target reports github_ok. Session: session_0156nqDt4ontnhzSFvT4PTB8

rows.title: DEPLOY-OIDC-1: deploys into the ultrastable account need no stored Cloudflare secret
rows.body: deploy-ultrastable.yml asks GitHub for this run's OIDC token (audience ultrastable-deploy) and posts flattened modules to ultrastable-site /__internal/deploy, which verifies the token (GitHub JWKS, repository ultrastable/ultrastable, ref main, unexpired) and uploads with its own CF_DEPLOY_TOKEN. deploy-workers.mjs and apply-d1-migrations.mjs exit without uploading when CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is a retired account (deploy/cloudflare-accounts.json). Session: session_0156nqDt4ontnhzSFvT4PTB8

rows.title: A loop's declared cadence must be the slowest producer's, and an empty metrics table is a finding
rows.body: First live reading of the ladder (2026-11-15 19:40 UTC): the watchdog producer on the site Worker runs hourly, so judging it at the tick's 10-minute cadence would file a false MISSED-watchdog; its cadence is now declared (DEFAULT_CADENCE) and the dashboard */10 cron is a faster second producer. The ladder also read 0 rows in the org metrics table: the live runtime was never seeded with liveness metrics, so measure has read nothing. IGNITE-instrumented files this with the numbers once looping holds.
